detailed_analysis: The raw AFM height map is dominated by a large low-frequency tilt/bow (RMS = 14.28 nm across a ~400 x 400 nm field), which is instrumental in origin (sample tilt plus scanner bow) rather than a real topographic feature. Plane fitting removes essentially all of this (RMS drops to 0.244 nm), and the additional row-median + per-column polynomial destripe brings the residual roughness down to Rq = 0.203 nm — sub-Angstrom-to-atomic-step scale corrugation. The leveled residual and square-resampled panels reveal the true structure: broad, flat terrace-like domains with sharp, straight edges oriented diagonally, consistent with layered/terraced material (the MoS2 substrate and/or peptide film patches) rather than a molecularly periodic lattice. The FFT log-power shows a strong diagonal power lobe and a cross of scan-line streaks, but no discrete reciprocal-lattice spots in the targeted 3-10 nm band. The single candidate reflection is weak (1.81 sigma, below significance) and the detected vertical feature at 0.0058 cyc/px (~134 nm period) is far outside any molecular self-assembly range — it is a slow scan-line/drift artifact and is correctly excluded. The diagonal FFT lobes correspond to residual diagonal streaks noted as a known leveling limitation, i.e., instrumental line-to-line correlation rather than a periodic monolayer motif. Net physical picture: the imaged surface consists of smooth, low-roughness terraced domains with no measurable in-plane periodic self-assembled peptide lattice at the resolution and length scales probed.

scientific_claims.claim: No resolvable periodic peptide self-assembly is detected in the 3-10 nm band; the only Fourier candidate is statistically insignificant (1.81 sigma) and the sub-Angstrom residual roughness (Rq = 0.20 nm) reflects smooth terraced domains rather than an ordered lattice.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Indicates that under these conditions the MoS2-binding peptide does not form a laterally ordered (crystalline/periodic) monolayer detectable by AFM, suggesting adsorption in a disordered, amorphous, or sub-resolution conformal film — an important negative constraint for engineering ordered biomolecular templates on 2D materials.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed the absence of long-range periodic ordering in MoS2-binding peptide films self-assembled on MoS2 as measured by AFM Fourier analysis?

analysis_approach: Convert to physical height, remove the dominant tilt (plane + per-row median) and resample to square pixels to expose the self-assembled peptide structure, then use targeted Fourier reflection mapping to detect and localize the characteristic self-assembly periodicity.

issues.problem: Faint residual diagonal streaks persist in the leveled image, matching the FFT diagonal power lobes.
